limitations: Player collision radius/half-width is not explicitly provided in the evidence; inference from wall contact at x = -0.75 assumes a typical 0.5 half-width.

assessment.title: The movement did not succeed; this may be a movement bug
assessment.playerImpact: None. The player attempted to move east at step -311 from position [-0.75, 1, -4.94] but the position did not change. The geometry shows a solid interior wall (wall-interior-1) at position [0, 1.25, -4] with size [0.5, 2.5, 2], spanning x ∈ [-0.25, 0.25] and z ∈ [-5, -3]. The player at z = -4.94 is within the wall's z-span. At x = -0.75 with a typical player half-width of ~0.5, the player's right edge reaches x = -0.25, exactly contacting the wall's left face. The prior east move at step -312 moved the player from x = -1.85 to x = -0.75 (Δx = +1.1), bringing the player into contact with the wall. The subsequent east input at step -311 correctly produced zero displacement because the solid wall blocks further eastward motion. The subsequent west move at step -310 succeeded (Δx = -1.55), confirming movement away from the wall works. This is expected collision behavior, not a movement defect.
assessment.rationale: The zero-displacement east move at step -311 is explained by collision with the solid interior wall at x ∈ [-0.25, 0.25], z ∈ [-5, -3]. The player reached the wall's left face at step -312 and could not penetrate it. Westward movement at step -310 succeeded normally. No defect is evidenced.

assessment.playerImpact: The player received appropriate feedback ('There is nothing to interact with here') when pressing interact while ~1.85 units away from the closed door. No progression block or incorrect behavior observed; the player simply moved away afterward.

The ~1.85m horizontal gap likely exceeds the interaction range, so the 'nothing to interact with' feedback is correct behavior. No state change occurred, and the player subsequently moved north away from the door. Without evidence of the intended interaction range or a closer attempt, this is expected feedback, not a defect.
